newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares driven to highs by new confidence.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares driven to highs by new confidence.

text.p: Turkey's stock market index ended at a record high on Thursday as confidence returned to a market plagued in recent months by political and economic worries after the election of an Islamist-led government, analysts said.

"I think the rally is going to gather further force. With the central bank in control of money, funds could flood into the market," said Atilla Yesilada, director of research at Global Securities in Istanbul.
The IMKB-100 index closed up 1.92 percent at 75,263.85, well above a previous all-time closing high of 74,730.36 in early July.
The uptrend was helped by hopes for an economic stability package supported by the International Monetary Fund and for an acceleration of the country's stalled privatisation process, Yesilada said.

However, analysts were sceptical about the degree to which the government of Islamist premier Necmettin Erbakan, criticised for populist policies since coming to power three months ago, will be able to stabilise the economy.

They looked to the release of September inflation data on Friday as a key indicator to the economic health of a country which has been struggling with 80 percent annual inflation and gaping budget and trade deficits.
Market expectations hover around a monthly rise of five percent.
"There is no improvement in the economy in general. But the prices were cheap," said Nalan Erkarakas, assistant to the general manager at Kentbank.
Positive expectations for corporate earnings in the second half and steady treasury bill and lira rates have provided the background to gains in recent sessions, analysts said.
"Recently the grip of both the treasury and the central bank was felt in the markets. This delayed any financial crisis expected to erupt in September," Erkarakas said.

Treasury bill yields rose slightly on lower liquidity on Thursday, with the average yield on the most heavily traded May 7 paper firming to 129.09 percent from 128.67 on Wednesday. The Turkish lira eased to 92,415 against the dollar from 92,075 at Wednesday's close.

Yesilada said sentiment had been helped by a successful start to the government's programme of issuing foreign-currency denominated debt, which had eased fears of a sharp rise in interest rates over the winter.
Deputy premier Tansu Ciller said on Wednesday Turkey would raise $2 billion by the end of the year through the issue of foreign currency-denominated bonds.
The positive market mood was reflected by a sharp rise in the daily trading volume to 24.52 trillion lira from 12.16 trillion a day earlier.
"Volumes have recovered fantastically. We can see the retail customer coming back and that is the main thing," Yesilada said.
Analysts said there were signs of international interest in Turkish shares, but this was limited to clients experienced in Turkey with new clients more difficult to attract.
Foreign investors remained cautious about Erbakan's coalition with Ciller's right-wing True Path Party, but forecast that technical factors will sustain the uptrend in the short-term.
